subject.title: [Bug]: cron.remove does not clean up session records in sessions.json

question: Should deleted cron jobs purge their base and run session rows immediately during cron.remove, or should deleted-job base rows be removed only by guarded retention cleanup?
rationale: Current main leaves rows behind, related proposed fixes use different cleanup timing, and base cron rows can carry persisted model/auth/label state that makes broad base-row deletion compatibility-sensitive.

options.title: Immediate Delete Cleanup
options.body: Make cron.remove purge the deleted job's base/run session rows and run history after the cron-store write succeeds, with per-agent and active-run safeguards.

options.title: Split Cleanup Scopes
options.body: Land guarded stale-orphan retention cleanup first, then keep this issue focused on whether immediate ghost-session cleanup is still required.

options.title: Retention-Only Cleanup
options.body: Treat deleted-job base rows as retention-managed state and accept that ghost rows may remain visible until the cutoff.

recommendation.title: Immediate Delete Cleanup
recommendation.body: Make cron.remove purge the deleted job's base/run session rows and run history after the cron-store write succeeds, with per-agent and active-run safeguards.

likelyOwner.reason: openperf owns the active overlapping PR that frames the guarded cron base-session cleanup semantics.
